chunks: And it has been narrated: “Indeed, crying over the deceased cuts off the salat (prayer), while crying at the remembrance of Paradise and the Fire is among the best of deeds in the salat (prayer).”

And it has been narrated: “There is nothing except that it has a measure or a weight, except crying out of the fear of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; for indeed a drop from it extinguishes seas of fires. And if one who weeps were to weep among a community, they would be shown mercy.”

key_terms.النِّيرَانِ: fires, referring to the fires of punishment
key_terms.الْقَطْرَةَ: a single drop, referring to a tear

ai.seo_question: Does crying during salat (prayer) invalidate it, and what is the virtue of weeping from fear of Allah?
ai.summary: This narration distinguishes between weeping that invalidates salat (prayer), such as crying over the deceased, and weeping that is spiritually praiseworthy in salat (prayer), such as crying from remembering Paradise and Hellfire. It also exalts tears shed from fear of Allah, presenting them as beyond ordinary measure and as a cause of divine mercy and protection from the Fire.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.941 - It has been narrated that "crying over a deceased person interrupts the prayer, but crying out of remembrance for Paradise and Hellfire is among the best deeds during prayer."

It is also narrated that "there is a measure or weight for everything except for tears shed out of the fear of Allah (swt), as a single drop of it can extinguish vast fires of Hell. And if a person who cries were present among a nation, they would be blessed with mercy."
